messages:
maria.song: Heads up — picked up an unusual burst of decrypts against a prod KMS key. Investigating, containment in progress. Drafting internal advisory + short exec blurb and a customer note. Need quick eyes.
kevin.li: Details? rule name, source IP, service-account?
maria.song: Alert: `kms.decrypt.burst` fired at 03:12 UTC. ~120 decrypt ops in 5m from 52.23.144.9. All requests used service account `svc-ingest-prod`. Logs attached (sanitized). No sign of key material export from KMS.
irene.m: Any evidence of lateral movement? Did the service account have other elevated roles?
maria.song: svc-ingest-prod had `roles/secret-retriever` + read-only S3. We just disabled the SA and rotated the SA keys. RBAC review in flight.
sec-bot: Incident created SEC-2026-03-12-01 by maria.song — severity: P2 — labels: kms, service-account, rotation-needed
kevin.li: Good. For the advisory we should call out: what we observed, immediate containment actions, impact (if any), and next steps (RBAC audit, log retention change). Keep language minimal for exec and clear for internal.
maria.song: Draft internal advisory below — please edit inline.

----- BEGIN INTERNAL ADVISORY DRAFT -----
What happened: At 03:12 UTC on 2026-03-12 our intrusion-detection rule flagged an anomalous burst of KMS Decrypt operations originating from a single external IP using the service account `svc-ingest-prod`.
Actions taken: We immediately disabled the service account, rotated the associated credentials, and rotated the affected customer-access KMS key version (no KMS key material left the HSM). We also increased audit log retention for KMS to 90 days for prod and enabled additional alerting on decrypt-rate anomalies.
Impact: We found no evidence that customer plaintext data was exfiltrated. No other accounts showed anomalous access.
Next steps: Complete RBAC review for svc-ingest-prod, push permanent rule to block the offending IP at the edge, and add a follow-up customer statement template.
Who to contact: security@redwood.internal or #eng-security for technical details.
----- END INTERNAL ADVISORY DRAFT -----

kevin.li: Suggest addition: timeline (detected, disabled, rotated) and a note about forensic artifacts preserved (snapshots of KMS audit logs and proxy logs) so legal/compliance can grab them. Also add action item to require MFA for any console/service account rotation workflows.
irene.m: For customer-facing language: be explicit that keys were not exposed, but recommend customers rotate any long-lived API tokens if they want extra assurance. Keep it reassuring. Draft suggestion below.
maria.song: Customer-facing draft: 

To our customers,
We detected an anomalous pattern of requests to our key-management system associated with an internal service account. We immediately disabled the account and rotated credentials and keys. Our investigation shows no evidence of customer data access or key material export. As a precaution, customers may rotate any long-lived API tokens; here is a short guide: https://redwood.internal/rotate-keys. We will follow up with any new findings.

kevin.li: Exec blurb for CTO: 
Quick summary: transient KMS decrypt anomaly tied to a single internal service account. Contained within 8 minutes via account disable + key rotation. No customer data exposure identified. Next steps: RBAC hardening, longer audit retention, and a smaller post-mortem in 48h.
maria.song: @cto can you ok the exec blurb?
cto: Looks fine. Please add estimated time to full RBAC audit (ETA 48 hours) and then send the internal advisory.
kevin.li: I'll add a note to the incident tracker to run vulnerability scan on the pod image that owned svc-ingest-prod and to confirm no leaked creds in repo history.
irene.m: Also recommend we push a short runbook for on-call to follow for KMS decrypt anomalies (disable SA, snapshot logs, rotate keys, notify customers if needed).
maria.song: Agree — I'll create the runbook PR and the customer notice template. Thanks for the reviews. Will send internal advisory at 12:05 UTC and ping execs.
kevin.li: :thumbsup:
sec-bot: SEC-2026-03-12-01 status updated -> contained by maria.song at 03:20 UTC
